area: Learned quadruped locomotion (RL sim2real, perceptive/wheel-legged locomotion, safe RL, world models, generalist and language-conditioned locomotion) - sweep dated 2026-10-19

papers.title: Hybrid Internal Model: Learning Agile Legged Locomotion with Simulated Robot Response (HIMLoco)
papers.key_idea: Single-stage estimator that infers terrain/disturbance from the robot's own response: an explicit velocity estimate plus a contrastively learned implicit stability latent, so no teacher-student split is needed.
papers.compute_needs: Reported ~1 h training on one RTX 4090; the MLP policy fits easily in 8 GB. The repo pins Isaac Gym Preview 4 + Python 3.7 + PyTorch 1.10, which cannot run on an RTX 5060 (sm_120), so it has to be ported to MJX/Isaac Lab.
papers.limitation: Blind (proprioception only). Tied to an Isaac Gym stack that NVIDIA confirms has no sm_120 kernels. Non-commercial license. Remains the standard estimator baseline.

papers.title: Real-DRL: Teach and Learn at Runtime
papers.key_idea: Runtime learning on the real plant: a DRL-Student learns while a physics-model PHY-Teacher backs up safety, a Trigger arbitrates, and safety-informed batch sampling handles corner cases. Validated on a real quadruped, an Isaac Gym quadruped and a cart-pole.
papers.compute_needs: Small DRL agent plus a model-based teacher. One 8 GB GPU should suffice for training and inference (estimate); learning runs on the robot.
papers.limitation: The PHY-Teacher needs a reasonably accurate physics model. The simulation part uses Isaac Gym, which does not run on Blackwell. Unclear whether it scales to agile or perceptive gaits.

papers.title: SPiDR: A Simple Approach for Zero-Shot Safety in Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.key_idea: Pessimistic domain randomization: folds the DR uncertainty about the sim-to-real gap into the safety constraints, which gives provable safe-transfer guarantees while staying a drop-in for standard DR + constrained-RL pipelines. Tested sim-to-sim and on two real robotic platforms.
papers.compute_needs: Same cost as constrained PPO with DR in a parallel simulator, so one 8 GB GPU is likely enough for legged tasks with a modest number of envs (estimate).
papers.limitation: The abstract does not name the real platforms, so legged hardware use is unconfirmed. The guarantee depends on the randomization covering the real system.

papers.title: DEAL: Diffusion Evolution Adversarial Learning for Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.key_idea: System identification: a discriminator scores how similar sim and real state transitions are, and that score is the fitness for diffusion evolution, which refines physical-parameter distributions from limited real data. Reported stable in high-dimensional parameter ID.
papers.compute_needs: Repeated batched sim rollouts plus a small discriminator. Feasible on one GPU (estimate). Needs only limited real data.
papers.limitation: The abstract does not name the robot platform. Identifies parameters only, with no residual model for unmodeled dynamics. Still requires real transition logs.

papers.title: Accelerating Visual-Policy Learning through Parallel Differentiable Simulation
papers.key_idea: Decouples rendering from the differentiable-simulation graph, so first-order analytic policy gradients can train visual policies without differentiable rendering. Less memory, smoother gradients, 4x final return on humanoid locomotion.
papers.compute_needs: Learned a humanoid running policy in 4 h on a single GPU, which makes it explicitly single-GPU friendly.
papers.limitation: Simulation only according to the abstract, with no real-robot deployment stated. Differentiable-sim gradients degrade on stiff, contact-rich terrain.

papers.title: GenPO: Generative Diffusion Models Meet On-Policy Reinforcement Learning
papers.key_idea: Brings diffusion policies into PPO-style on-policy RL. Exact diffusion inversion plus a doubled dummy-action trick makes the action mapping invertible, giving exact log-likelihoods and unbiased entropy/KL. Aimed at massively parallel IsaacLab training.
papers.compute_needs: More compute per step than a Gaussian MLP, but likely fits in 8 GB with fewer envs (estimate).
papers.limitation: Main results are IsaacLab simulation benchmarks; real deployment is not stated in the abstract. Diffusion inference latency matters for onboard control.

papers.title: Periodic Skill Discovery (PSD)
papers.key_idea: Unsupervised skill discovery that maps states to a circular latent space whose radius encodes temporal distance, giving periodic gait-like skills with controllable periods. Works from pixels, combines with METRA, and helps on downstream tasks such as hurdling.
papers.compute_needs: Light: MuJoCo-style tasks, trainable on a single GPU.
papers.limitation: Walker2D/HalfCheetah-type benchmarks only, no quadruped hardware. Useful mainly as an example of how a pure-algorithm locomotion paper gets into NeurIPS.

papers.title: Latent Adaptation of Foundation Policies for Sim-to-Real Transfer (Found-adapt)
papers.key_idea: Pretrains a foundation policy on unlabeled offline sim trajectories as reusable skills. At deployment it does not retrain the policy; a small parameter-efficient adapter refines only the latent from a little target-domain data.
papers.compute_needs: Adapter-only adaptation, similar to LoRA in spirit. Adaptation and probably pretraining fit on one 8 GB GPU (estimate).
papers.limitation: The abstract reports 'multiple locomotion tasks and dynamic variations' and does not clearly mention a real quadruped. Depends on how well the offline data covers the target dynamics.

papers.title: Empowering Multi-Robot Cooperation via Sequential World Models (SeqWM)
papers.key_idea: Each agent has an autoregressive world model that predicts its own trajectory conditioned on its predecessors' predictions, which amounts to explicit intention sharing. Tested on Bi-DexHands and Multi-Quadruped (gate, push-box, shepherd) and deployed on real Unitree Go2-W wheel-legged robots.
papers.compute_needs: Per-agent world models (TD-MPC2/HARL/M3W base). Likely one GPU for small teams (estimate). The repo uses Isaac Gym + Python 3.8, so it must be ported for Blackwell.
papers.limitation: Needs several robots. Cooperation is learned at a high level, not joint-level locomotion. Isaac Gym dependency.

papers.title: CE-Nav: Flow-Guided Reinforcement Refinement for Cross-Embodiment Local Navigation
papers.key_idea: IL-then-RL. An embodiment-agnostic normalizing-flow expert (VelFlow) is trained offline on classical-planner data to output multimodal velocity commands; a lightweight dynamics-aware refiner is then learned online for each new robot. Quadrupeds, bipeds and quadrotors, with real deployments.
papers.compute_needs: Offline flow expert plus a lightweight RL refiner. Probably fits on a single GPU (estimate).
papers.limitation: Works at the velocity-command level and assumes an existing locomotion controller. That also makes it suitable for robots whose SDK only accepts velocity commands.

papers.title: WestWorld: A Knowledge-Encoded Scalable Trajectory World Model for Diverse Robotic Systems
papers.key_idea: Trajectory world model built from a system-aware mixture of experts routed by a learned system embedding, plus a structural (morphology) embedding. Pretrained on 89 environments; improves zero/few-shot prediction and MPPI control; deployed on a real Unitree Go1.
papers.compute_needs: Pretrained checkpoints are released, so fine-tuning and inference on 8 GB look feasible (estimate). The stack is PyTorch 2.4.1 + mujoco-py/MuJoCo 2.1, which must be upgraded for sm_120.
papers.limitation: Proprioceptive trajectory model with no terrain perception. The Go1 demo shows 'stable locomotion', not agile skills. MPPI adds onboard compute.

papers.title: Learning Anisotropic Value Geometry with Finsler Reinforcement Learning (FiRL)
papers.key_idea: Locomotion cost is a direction-dependent Finsler metric F(x,v) (uphill/downhill, lateral slip), optimized under CVaR with a provably contractive Bellman operator. On a 12-degree sloped Hopper: over 35% lower worst-case impact force and 15% less energy. Includes real-robot trials.
papers.compute_needs: Small actor-critic, single-GPU friendly (estimate).
papers.limitation: Headline results are on a simplified Hopper; the real robot is not named in the abstract. An earlier version was desk-rejected at ICLR 2026.

papers.title: Adaptive Reinforcement Learning for Unobservable Random Delays (ACDA)
papers.key_idea: An 'interaction layer' where the agent emits a matrix of future actions spanning a delay horizon, which handles unobservable, time-varying delays and lost packets. Model-based actor-critic with delay adaptation; beats SOTA on locomotion benchmarks, including with real measured delays.
papers.compute_needs: Small model-based RL, trainable on a single GPU (estimate).
papers.limitation: Simulated locomotion benchmarks only, with no legged hardware. That gap is directly relevant to high-latency SDK robots.

papers.title: MuJoCo Playground
papers.venue_year: arXiv 2502.08844 (Feb 2025; no venue on arXiv page)
papers.key_idea: Open-source MJX/JAX framework (physics + batch renderer + envs, optional MuJoCo Warp backend). Zero-shot sim-to-real on Go1 (joystick, handstand, footstand, fall recovery), Berkeley Humanoid, G1, T1, LEAP hand and Franka, from state and from pixels.
papers.compute_needs: Go1 flat-terrain joystick trains in about 5 min on 2x RTX 4090; ~417K PPO steps/s on one A100. On a 5060 8 GB, expect tens of minutes (estimate). Needs Python 3.10+ and jax[cuda12]; sm_120 support not verified.
papers.limitation: The MJX contact model is less battle-tested than PhysX on complex terrain. No formal leaderboard.

papers.title: Isaac Lab: A GPU-Accelerated Simulation Framework for Multi-Modal Robot Learning
papers.key_idea: Successor to Isaac Gym on Isaac Sim: GPU-parallel PhysX, RTX sensors, a modular API, RL and IL, and sim-to-real tooling. The default framework for legged RL in 2025-2026; GenPO, NaVILA's benchmarks and FastTD3 all use it.
papers.compute_needs: Isaac Sim minimum spec is an RTX 4080 with 16 GB VRAM and 32 GB RAM on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 (20.04 not listed). Headless proprioceptive locomotion with fewer envs may still run on 8 GB (unverified estimate). Docker is the workaround for 20.04.
papers.limitation: Heavy stack. Camera-based or perceptive training with many envs is hard on 8 GB. Isaac Gym, its predecessor, is dead on Blackwell (no sm_120 kernels per NVIDIA).

papers.title: Open-DiffLoco: Open-Source Differentiable Learning for Deployable Blind Quadruped Locomotion
papers.key_idea: First open-source framework for deployable locomotion via differentiable simulation (SHAC in MJX). Blind omnidirectional velocity tracking on a real Unitree Go2 with RMSE under 0.2 m/s, speeds over 1 m/s, and robustness to pushes and uneven terrain. Builds on CoRL 2024 'Learning Quadruped Locomotion Using Differentiable Simulation'.
papers.compute_needs: About 20-60 min on one RTX 5080 using under 6 GB VRAM. The closest documented match to an RTX 5060 8 GB.
papers.limitation: Blind only. Single author, not peer reviewed. Contact gradients still limit agile or perceptive skills.

papers.title: FastTD3: Simple, Fast, and Capable RL for Humanoid Control (+ follow-up 'Learning Sim-to-Real Humanoid Locomotion in 15 Minutes', arXiv 2512.01996)
papers.key_idea: Off-policy TD3/SAC made fast with massively parallel envs, large batches, a distributional critic and tuned hyperparameters. The follow-up FastSAC/FastTD3 recipe uses minimal rewards and heavy DR for G1/T1 sim-to-real.
papers.compute_needs: HumanoidBench in under 3 h on one A100; G1/T1 sim-to-real in about 15 min on one RTX 4090. Replay buffers use a lot of VRAM, so 8 GB needs smaller buffers/batches (estimate).
papers.limitation: Validated mainly on humanoids; quadruped sim-to-real with these recipes is less documented. Off-policy hyperparameters are sensitive.

papers.title: LocoFormer: Generalist Locomotion via Long-context Adaptation
papers.key_idea: Omni-bodied policy trained with large-scale RL on procedurally generated legged and wheeled robots under heavy DR. Its context spans episode boundaries, so it adapts in context to unseen kinematics, weight changes and motor failures, and improves after falls.
papers.compute_needs: Described as 'massive scale RL'; training likely needs a cluster, while inference of the transformer policy likely fits in 8 GB (both estimates).
papers.limitation: Training cannot be reproduced on one 8 GB GPU. The abstract page does not name the real robots.

papers.title: Towards Embodiment Scaling Laws in Robot Locomotion
papers.key_idea: Trains one policy on about 1,000 procedurally generated embodiments that vary in topology, geometry and kinematics. Generalization scales positively with the number of embodiments, more than with extra data on fixed bodies. Zero-shot transfer to a real Unitree Go2 and H1.
papers.compute_needs: Training compute not stated; large-scale training implied, inference cheap.
papers.code: project site https://embodiment-scaling-laws.github.io/ (no repo on abstract page)
papers.limitation: Expensive to reproduce; blind locomotion. A pretrained generalist could still serve as a prior for an unusual robot.

papers.title: LocoVLM: Grounding Vision and Language for Adapting Versatile Legged Locomotion Policies
papers.key_idea: An LLM builds an instruction-grounded locomotion skill database; a VLM maps scene semantics to real-time skill advice; a style-conditioned policy executes it. Up to 87% instruction-following accuracy with no online calls to cloud foundation models.
papers.compute_needs: Language layer is training-free (frozen pretrained models); only the style policy needs RL. Local inference on 8 GB is plausible with a small or quantized VLM (estimate).
papers.limitation: Bounded by a fixed skill library. The abstract page does not name the VLM or robot. Not peer reviewed.

papers.title: NaVILA: Legged Robot Vision-Language-Action Model for Navigation
papers.venue_year: arXiv 2412.04453 (v2 Feb 2025); OpenReview shows 'Submitted to ICLR 2025' with no accept tag
papers.key_idea: Two-level VLN: a VLA outputs mid-level spatial language commands (for example 'moving forward 75cm') that a vision-based RL locomotion policy executes. Adds IsaacLab VLN benchmarks with realistic scenes and low-level control, plus real-robot experiments.
papers.compute_needs: VLA fine-tuning needs multiple GPUs. 8 GB inference would need aggressive quantization or a cloud model (estimate).
papers.limitation: Heavy VLA. The low-level skill interface is fixed. Not accepted at ICLR 2025 according to OpenReview status.

papers.title: World Model-based Perception for Visual Legged Locomotion (WMP)
papers.key_idea: Replaces teacher-student distillation with a world model trained entirely in sim; the policy acts on its latent. The world model predicts real trajectories accurately and beats SOTA on traversability and robustness in sim and real. A 2026 follow-up (arXiv 2609.29092) adds depth-denoising world models for noisy-depth parkour.
papers.compute_needs: World model plus RL in a parallel sim. Single-GPU feasibility not verified (estimate: moderate).
papers.limitation: Venue not confirmed on the arXiv page. Real depth noise is an open problem, which is exactly what the 2026 follow-up targets.

papers.title: ATRos: Learning Energy-Efficient Agile Locomotion for Wheeled-legged Robots
papers.key_idea: Hybrid walking-driving RL with no predefined gaits. A prediction network infers environment state from proprioception and feeds the actor-critic, aiming at agility and energy efficiency. Real tests on flat ground, stairs and grass.
papers.compute_needs: Blind MLP policy; single-GPU feasible (estimate).
papers.limitation: 4-page workshop paper. The robot is not named and the abstract gives no quantitative real-world numbers. A sign that wheel-legged RL is still immature.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning on Cost-Constrained Quadrupedal Hardware
papers.key_idea: Actuator lag over 50 ms makes locomotion on cheap hardware partially observable. A forward model of mean actuator delay plus a time-aware network produces an emergent CPG-like rhythm that tolerates +320 ms latency perturbations on a Mini Pupper 2.
papers.compute_needs: Small, low-DoF policy; trivial on 8 GB (estimate).
papers.limitation: Models only the mean delay; toy-scale platform; no venue. Highly relevant if the user's SDK has high latency.

papers.title: Simulator Adaptation for Sim-to-Real Learning of Legged Locomotion via Proprioceptive Distribution Matching
papers.key_idea: Compares hardware and sim rollouts as distributions of joint observations and actions, so no time alignment or mocap is needed. Used as a black-box objective for parameter ID, action-delta models or residual actuator models. Reduced drift on a real Go2 (including a bipedal gait) with under 5 min of hardware data.
papers.compute_needs: Black-box optimization over batched sim plus about 5 min of real logs. Likely one GPU (estimate).
papers.limitation: arXiv only; Go2 only; untested with perception or wheels.

benchmarks.name: MuJoCo Playground locomotion suite (Go1 joystick flat/rough, handstand, footstand, fall recovery; G1/T1/Berkeley Humanoid joystick)
benchmarks.simulator: MuJoCo MJX (JAX); optional MuJoCo Warp backend (--impl warp)
benchmarks.metrics: Episode reward, linear/yaw velocity tracking error, real-world success, wall-clock and steps/s
benchmarks.sota_note: Go1 joystick in about 5 min on 2x RTX 4090; ~417K PPO steps/s (Go1 flat) on one A100. No formal leaderboard; papers compare wall-clock to a given policy quality.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Designed for one GPU; 8 GB should work with fewer envs (estimate); JAX on sm_120 needs checking

benchmarks.name: Isaac Lab legged velocity-tracking tasks (flat/rough procedural terrain, ANYmal/Unitree)
benchmarks.simulator: Isaac Lab on Isaac Sim (PhysX GPU)
benchmarks.metrics: Mean return, terrain-curriculum level, velocity tracking error, fall/timeout rate, torque/energy
benchmarks.sota_note: De facto standard for 2025-2026 legged RL (GenPO, NaVILA benchmarks, FastTD3 evals); comparisons are against PPO baselines, with no unified leaderboard.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Official minimum RTX 4080 16 GB on Ubuntu 22.04/24.04; 8 GB headless proprioceptive training with fewer envs is an unverified estimate

benchmarks.name: Classic MuJoCo/DMC/Gymnasium locomotion (Hopper, Walker2D, HalfCheetah, Ant, Humanoid)
benchmarks.metrics: Return, sample efficiency, CVaR/worst-case cost, energy
benchmarks.sota_note: The testbed used by CCF-A algorithm papers in this sweep (PSD, FiRL, ACDA, WestWorld MPPI, Partially Equivariant RL at ICLR 2026). Accepted papers pair gains here with optional real-robot validation.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: CPU or one small GPU; cheapest option

benchmarks.name: HumanoidBench
benchmarks.sota_note: FastTD3 solves many tasks in under 3 h on one A100. Peripheral for quadrupeds but the standard speed reference for off-policy RL.

benchmarks.name: Robust Gymnasium (ICLR 2025 poster)
benchmarks.metrics: Return under observation, action and dynamics perturbations
benchmarks.sota_note: Useful for stress-testing robustness claims in a general-RL paper; locomotion tasks included.

benchmarks.name: Legged VLN in IsaacLab (NaVILA benchmarks) plus real-world VLN embodied-gap evaluation (ICCV 2025 'Rethinking the Embodied Gap in VLN')
benchmarks.simulator: IsaacLab with realistic scenes and low-level locomotion
benchmarks.metrics: Success rate, SPL, navigation error, falls/collisions
benchmarks.sota_note: NaVILA reports gains over prior VLN methods. The ICCV 2025 study finds large real-robot drops from limited FOV, lighting changes, collisions and falls.
benchmarks.gpu_needs: Rendering plus VLA training exceeds 8 GB; inference via API or quantized model (estimate)

benchmarks.name: Real-robot locomotion protocol (de facto, not a formal benchmark)
benchmarks.metrics: Velocity RMSE, max speed, success on stairs/slope/grass, push survived, falls per km, cost of transport, joint temperature, minutes of real data used
benchmarks.sota_note: Examples: Open-DiffLoco Go2 RMSE under 0.2 m/s and over 1 m/s; Go2-W covered about 2.8 km at Tsukuba Challenge 2025 without overheating stops (arXiv 2606.21387).

trends: Simulator shift: Isaac Gym/legged_gym is legacy. NVIDIA confirms Isaac Gym Preview 4 has no sm_120 kernels and there is no workaround, so migrate to Isaac Lab. MJX/MuJoCo Playground, MuJoCo Warp and Genesis (Apache-2.0, Python 3.10-3.13; README makes no speed claims, tech-report blog May 2026) are the alternatives.

Training-time collapse: off-policy massively parallel RL (FastTD3/FastSAC) gives about 15-min humanoid sim2real on one RTX 4090, and differentiable simulation (SHAC in MJX) gives a deployable Go2 policy in 20-60 min under 6 GB VRAM. Single consumer GPUs are now credible for locomotion research.

Generative (diffusion/flow) policies trained with online RL are a hot CCF-A topic using locomotion as a testbed: GenPO and ReinFlow (NeurIPS 2025), FPO++ (ICLR 2026 submission), and RFO and DADP (ICML 2026).

Cross-embodiment generalist locomotion via procedural morphology randomization and long context: LocoFormer, Embodiment Scaling Laws (~1,000 bodies), URMAv2 (50 robots, millions of variations), and cross-humanoid WBC at ICML 2026. Training is cluster-scale; the pretrained policies are cheap to run.

Safety/robustness with theory is the reliable CCF-A route: SPiDR (provably safe DR), Real-DRL (physics teacher plus runtime learning on a real quadruped), FiRL (CVaR-Finsler Bellman) and ACDA (random delays), at NeurIPS 2025 and ICML 2026, typically with theory, sim benchmarks and a modest real demo.

Data-efficient real2sim calibration is replacing blind DR: DEAL (NeurIPS 2025), proprioceptive distribution matching (under 5 min of Go2 data), actuator-delay forward models for cheap robots, and latent adapters (Found-adapt, ICLR 2026) instead of retraining the policy.

World models used for perception and control: WMP (visual locomotion), depth-denoising world models for parkour (arXiv 2609.29092), SeqWM multi-quadruped (ICLR 2026), WestWorld MoE trajectory world model with Go1 MPPI (ICML 2026 spotlight).

Language/VLM layers on top of locomotion skills: LocoVLM (87% instruction following, no cloud calls), NaVILA (VLA mid-level commands to an RL controller), MobileVLA-R1. The ICCV 2025 embodied-gap study shows big real-world drops for legged VLN.

Wheel-legged quadrupeds are an emerging but immature niche: ATRos, recovery-aware navigation on a low-cost wheeled quadruped, Go2-W 2.8 km navigation with thermal-aware load sharing, AWARE reflexive evasion. Mostly IROS 2025 workshop or arXiv level, and SeqWM used real Go2-W.

Venue reality (official CCF 2026 list, 7th edition, March 2026): A-class AI conferences are AAAI, NeurIPS, ACL, CVPR, ICCV, ICML, ICLR. ICRA is B, IROS is C, IJCAI and ECCV are B, T-RO is B, and RSS/CoRL/RA-L/IJRR/Science Robotics are not listed. ACM MM and SIGGRAPH are A (multimedia); TPAMI/IJCV/AI/JMLR and SCIS are A journals.

Pattern from OpenReview status (inference): system-style quadruped papers at ICLR 2025 (NaVILA, Constrained Skill Discovery, RL from Wild Animal Videos, Neural Circuit Priors) show only 'Submitted', while accepted ICLR/NeurIPS/ICML locomotion work is framed as a general learning algorithm.
open_gaps: Minute-scale proprioceptive real2sim (distribution matching or DEAL-style) combined with provable safe transfer (SPiDR) and runtime safety (Real-DRL) has not been shown together on a commercial wheel-legged or SDK-limited quadruped. A strong NeurIPS/ICML-style story.

Unobservable, time-varying delay on real 12-16 DoF legged robots: ACDA is sim-only with recorded delays and the cost-constrained paper uses a Mini Pupper with mean delay only. Delay-adaptive locomotion on real hardware with non-stationary SDK latency is open.

Test-time latent or adapter adaptation (Found-adapt, LocoFormer-style context) has not been demonstrated on real quadrupeds or wheel-legged robots with LoRA-scale updates and a few minutes of data. Fits a one-GPU budget.

No standard wheel-legged benchmark: energy, leg/wheel mode switching, hip-motor thermal load (the Go2-W overheating issue) and fall recovery are reported ad hoc in workshop papers. A reproducible sim suite plus real protocol plus an algorithm is open.

Closed-loop, failure-aware VLM-to-gait grounding: current systems pick from fixed skills (LocoVLM, NaVILA), while real VLN on legged robots degrades from falls and collisions (ICCV 2025). Uncertainty-aware VLM override of speed, height and gait under a safety filter is missing.

Risk-sensitive or anisotropic objectives (FiRL's Finsler + CVaR) are only shown on a sloped Hopper. Extending them to real quadruped slopes, stairs and grass with direction-dependent energy and impact metrics is open.

Generative (diffusion/flow) RL policies under onboard latency budgets: GenPO and FPO++ are rarely tested on cheap onboard compute. Few-step or distilled flow policies for real-time quadruped control are open.

Perceptive differentiable-sim locomotion on real quadrupeds: Open-DiffLoco is blind and the NeurIPS 2025 visual differentiable-sim work stays in sim. A depth-based variant trained on one consumer GPU is open.
Sim-trained world models (WMP, WestWorld) are rarely reused as real-time fall or failure predictors that trigger recovery or a safe stop. Cheap to try with pretrained checkpoints.
low_compute_entry_points: First, confirm the LTR M1 SDK level: joint position/torque commands at 50 Hz or more, IMU, timestamps. The exact model could not be identified. If only velocity commands are exposed, pivot to navigation, VLM or safety-filter work (CE-Nav-style refiners) rather than joint-level RL.

Stack on the RTX 5060 (sm_120): do not use Isaac Gym/legged_gym (no sm_120 kernels). Use MuJoCo Playground/MJX (Python 3.10+, jax[cuda12]; verify sm_120) in a venv or Docker, or Isaac Lab headless in an Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 container. Host 20.04 is unsupported, and 8 GB is below Isaac Sim's 16 GB minimum.

Fast baseline: reproduce Open-DiffLoco (SHAC in MJX, under 6 GB, 20-60 min on an RTX 5080) or a Playground Go1 joystick policy, then swap in your robot's MJCF/URDF. Port a HIMLoco-style estimator as the second baseline.

CCF-A framing: propose a general RL/sim2real algorithm (delay adaptation, safe DR, latent test-time adaptation, distribution-matching ID) and evaluate on classic MuJoCo, Playground/Isaac Lab legged tasks, and your real robot, following Real-DRL/SPiDR/Found-adapt/ACDA. Small networks are fine on 8 GB.

Minimal-data system ID: log about 5 min of proprioception from the real robot, fit sim parameters or a residual actuator model with distribution matching, and report drift and velocity RMSE before and after. A cheap, publishable component.

Training-free language layer for AAAI/ACM MM/CVPR angles: a cloud VLM API or a 4-bit 3-8B local VLM maps instructions and images to gait, speed and height parameters of a style-conditioned policy (LocoVLM-style). The VRAM fit on 8 GB is an estimate.
Pretrained world model: fine-tune the WestWorld HF checkpoint on your robot's logs as a fall predictor or MPPI baseline. PyTorch 2.4.1 must be upgraded to a CUDA 12.8+ build for Blackwell.
Budget: an RTX 5060 is likely several times slower than a 4090/5080 (estimate), so plan 1-4 h for runs reported at 15-60 min. 32 GB RAM limits replay-buffer size for FastTD3/FastSAC.

Venue choice: ICRA (B), IROS (C) and CoRL/RSS (unlisted) do not count as CCF-A in the 2026 list. Target ICLR/NeurIPS/ICML/AAAI/CVPR/ICCV/ACM MM with an algorithm-first framing, or the SCIS journal (CCF-A).
